04/04/2020

Dr Tony Jones
Private Practice
12 New Street
Stillwater

Dear Dr Jones,
Re: Ms Betty Johnson, aged 81
I am writing to update you about your patient Ms Johnson who has been operated for right total knee replacement. She requires your follow-up of her blood tests.
On 25/02/2015, after the operation, Ms Johnson was vitally stable .However, her blood tests revealed anaemia for which blood transfusion was done. On the first day post the operation, she was commenced on  paracetamol 665mg two tablets three times a day ,warfarin 5 mg orally , Clexan 80 mg subcutaneously and Feretab 300mg at morning.
Over the next two weeks, Ms Johnson`s condition has been improved, she has been able to mobilize with crutches assistance , her wound has been cured and clips has been removed ,here  haemoglobine has been increased up to 111g/l ,and Clexane was ceased on the sixth day .Ms Johnson was transferred to rehabilitation center on 07/02/2015.
During the rehabilitation period, Ms Johnson has been more dependent, her ECG and X-ray were normal and her pathology has revealed haemoglobin elevation up to 112g/l and INR of 3.5 .therefore, warfarin and Feretabe doses has been decreased.
As for a discharge plan today with home nurse assistance, I would be grateful if you could repeat FBE and INR tests in a one-week. Please note, a rehabilitation appointment was scheduled in two weeks and a list of her home medications were attached to my letter. Should be any further queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.
Yours sincerely,
Doctor
